about: Fixes applied on top of the source snapshots at import (python db.py --reset). Keyed by Yale Pitchbook id. Admin edits to imported listings are saved here automatically.

111.name: Home Catalyst Partners
111.tagline: Real estate investment firm delivering risk-adjusted returns through triple-bottom-line housing opportunities.
111.reason: Pitchbook listed it as healthcare housing for adults with autism/IDD. It is a real estate investment firm; housing for adults with autism/IDD (64 units) is one of its deals, not its focus.

19.name: Win Number
19.tagline: Win Number provides campaign planning, voter-contact tracking, analytics, and reporting tools for small to medium-sized campaigns.
19.reason: The Technology industry fits the campaign software and analytics offering. However, the homepage describes planning, tracking, and reporting tools, not an all-in-one AI platform or a Democratic-only focus, so the pitch should be revised. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

29.name: VeruStruct
29.tagline: Verustruct develops robotic construction systems that automate building affordable, sustainable housing.
29.reason: The listing broadly reflects Verustruct's focus on robotic construction for affordable, sustainable housing, but its specific claims about upcycled materials and chamber-based printing are not supported by the homepage. The site's stated approach is automated formwork, robotics, conventional structural materials, and translational slipform. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

36.name: Vault Kinetics Inc.
36.tagline: Vault Kinetics makes portable force plates and analysis software for measuring human performance.
36.reason: The listing's 'intelligent flooring' pitch is misleading: the site describes portable force-plate hardware and performance analysis tools. Technology fits, but Health & Biotech better reflects its human-performance focus. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

99.name: Urologic Design
99.tagline: Urologic Design is developing a non-surgical urethral occlusion device to help men manage stress urinary incontinence.
99.reason: The pitch is broadly aligned with the site, though it describes Uroplug as a current device rather than one under development. Health & Biotech fits; Climate & Sustainability is not a primary industry—the waste-reduction benefit is secondary to the continence-care product. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

17.name: Suppal
17.tagline: Suppal is a marketplace where creators remake proven viral video formats for brands and earn based on the views they generate.
17.reason: The listing describes an admissions-support product for high school students, but the website presents Suppal as a marketplace for creators to remake viral videos for brands. Education does not fit the website's stated main business. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

78.name: Sláinte Health
78.tagline: Sláinte is a wellness app that recommends one small health habit and connects people with nearby in-person activities and programs.
78.reason: The listing broadly identifies a consumer wellness product, but its claim that it uses everyday data for personalized next steps is not supported by the site, which emphasizes gentle suggestions and nearby activities. The site describes general wellness, not medical care. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

101.name: Pro-Patient Tech
101.tagline: Pro-Patient Tech provides personalized, goal-oriented health guidance and connects patients with clinicians and health resources.
101.reason: The listing describes a condition-specific lifestyle recommendation database, but the website presents Caspia as a team of specialized health agents offering personalized health guidance. Health & Biotech fits; Technology is also relevant to the platform. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

60.name: Playbl
60.tagline: Playbl provides evidence-based digital health games that help adolescents make healthier choices.
60.reason: The pitch captures Playbl’s focus on youth health and substance-use prevention, but narrows its work to vaping and opioids and frames it mainly as a consumer offering. The site describes a broader portfolio of evidence-based digital health games for schools and youth-facing organizations. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

4.name: Mundaly
4.tagline: Mundaly helps companies monetize anonymized data and helps AI labs source globally representative real-world data.
4.reason: The website describes Mundaly as a marketplace/licensing service for company data used by AI labs, not an AI platform for community engagement or impact measurement. Technology fits; the listed Health & Biotech industry is not supported by the homepage. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

92.name: Orphic
92.tagline: Orphic provides a platform for managing the lifecycle of protection products across vehicles, equipment, and appliances.
92.reason: The pitch does not match the website’s stated offering, which centers on protection products. Technology remains a fitting industry classification. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

90.name: General Neuro
90.tagline: General Neuro makes a wearable headband that applies gentle electrical stimulation during reading practice for children with dyslexia.
90.reason: The pitch is misleading: the website describes NeuroLingo as a headband used during reading practice for struggling readers, not a device to reopen a critical period for language acquisition. The listed industries are broadly consistent with the product’s health, education, and technology aspects. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

5.name: Kenji Health
5.tagline: Kenji uses AI to engage participants in community care programs and measure their outcomes.
5.reason: The industries broadly fit the site’s focus on health programs, AI technology, and community impact. The pitch is vague and does not capture the specific offering: AI-powered participant engagement and outcomes measurement for community care programs. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

48.name: Cybrexa Therapeutics
48.tagline: Cybrexa develops targeted intracellular delivery of anti-cancer agents.
48.reason: The Health & Biotech industry fits, but the pitch describes a different approach than the website’s stated focus on targeted intracellular delivery of anti-cancer agents. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

102.name: EnerBot
102.tagline: EnerBot provides engineering, procurement, and deployment support for tailored renewable energy projects and technologies.
102.reason: The website supports the clean-energy focus, but describes EnerBot primarily as an energy project engineering, procurement, and construction company, rather than specifically as a provider of the listed product categories. Education and Robotics are not supported as industries; Climate & Sustainability and Technology fit the site. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

77.name: Crew Dog
77.tagline: Crew Dog creates original hand-drawn, embroidered collegiate apparel and custom designs for universities, groups, and teams.
77.reason: Consumer is an appropriate industry, but the pitch is too vague: Crew Dog primarily sells hand-drawn, embroidered collegiate apparel and offers custom designs. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)

122.name: Caela Enterprises
122.tagline: Caela Enterprises offers storytelling, creative consulting, brand strategy, and art, including its own book.
122.reason: Media & Entertainment fits the creative work, but the site presents Caela as an author, storytelling and brand strategist, creative consultant, and artist. It does not substantiate the listing's claim of a multigenerational publishing, education, and entertainment franchise. (Found by the Listing Auditor; approved by an admin.)
